P1.quote: Schema per tenant | Logical, but each request must switch to the right schema | 200 schemas × 30 tables = **6,000 tables**. Every migration runs 200 times, and partial failures leave tenants on different versions | Only slightly safer, at a much higher running cost

P2.quote: Database per tenant | Physical | 200 databases to back up, monitor, migrate and pool connections for | Too much to run, except as a paid enterprise option (see below)

P3.quote: The tenant always comes from the **authenticated session**. Never take it from the request body, URL or headers.

P4.quote: Enforce the separation in two places: the application, and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) as a safety net.

P5.quote: **Cross-tenant tests** for every endpoint and job: tenant A's user can't read, update, delete or reference tenant B's data, and a tenant ID supplied by the client is ignored.

P6.quote: Don't say "physically separated" or "fully separate databases" unless you sell the dedicated tier. Customers often check those claims in security questionnaires.

P7.quote: I haven't written any code or files.
